FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 27 April 1 989, after the 
draft finalized by the Small Tools Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical 
Engineering Division Council, 

In the preparation of this standard, considerable assistance has been derived from: 

ISO 3438 : 1975 Subland twist drill with morse taper shanks for holes prior to tapping screw thread. 
International Standards Organization ( ISO ). 

DIN 8379 : 1981 Subland twist drill with morse taper shanks for holes prior to tapping screw thread. 
Deutches Institut furNormung ( DIN ). 

This standard applies for subland twist drills for producing holes and countersink prior to tapping 
coarse pitch screw threads. For fine pitch screw threads refer to note given in Table 1. 

The other Indian Standards in this series are: 

Is 12688: 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with morse taper shanks for clearance 
holes and countersinks for countersunk head screws — Specification 

IS 12689: 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with parallel shank for clearance holes 
and counterbores for slotted cheese head screw — Specification 

IS 12690 : 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with morse taper shanks for clearance holes 
and counterbores for slotted cheese head screw — Specification 

IS 12691 : 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with parallel shanks for holes prior to 
tapping screw threads — Specification 

IS 12692:1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with parallel shanks for clearance holes 
and countersink for countersunk head screws — Specification

SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

!•! This standard covers dimensions and other 
requirements for the subland twist drills with 
mprse taper shanks for producing holes and 
countersinks prior to tapping screw threads M 8 
to M 30 ( coarse pitch ) conforming to IS 10952 : 
1984. 

2 REFERENCES 

tSNo. 
IS 1715: 1986 



IS 5099 : 1983

3 TERMINOLOGY 

3.1 For the purpose of this standard, the defini- 
tions given in IS 10915 : 1984 shall apply. 

4 DIMENSIONS 

4*1 Dimensions of subland twist drill shall be 
&8 given in Table 1. 

AJl Tolerances 

The tolerance on the flute length /i and overall 
length / shall be ±5 mm. 

5 MATERIAL 

5.1 The material of subland twist drills shall 
be as given in IS S099 : 1983. 

6 HARDNESS 

6.1 The hardness of subland twist drill shall be 
as given in IS 5099 : 1983. 



7 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

7.1 Tool Type 'N', right hand cutting will be 
supplied unless otherwise specified. 

7.2 The diameter d and di shall be measured as 
near to the point as practicable. 

7.3 While using this drill, cutting speed should 
be selected according to the large dia *d' and the 
feed rate according to small ( pilot ) diameter 'rf/. 

7.4 For requirements not covered in this standard 
it shall conform to the requirements as given in 
IS 5099: 1983. 

8 PROTECTIVE COATING 

8.1 Protective coating on subland twist drill 
shall be as given in IS 5099 : 1983. 

9 SAMPLING 

9.1 The sampling and criteria of acceptance 
shall be in accordance with IS 7778 : 1975. 

10 TEST 

10.1 Subland twist drills shall be tested accord- 
ing to IS 5099 : 1983. 

11 DESIGNATION 

11.1 A subland twist drill with morse taper 
shank having diameter d '=* \6 mm and step 
diameter ^1 :== 120 mm, of Tool Type 'N* for 
right hand cutting, made from high speed steel 
and conforming to this standard shall be designed 
as: 

Subland Twist Drill 160 x 120 IS 12687 

11.2 When required with tool type other than 
'N', *H' or *S' should be added in the designation 
after the diameter as appropriate. 

12 MARKING 

12.1 Subland twist drill shall be marked as given 
in IS 5099 : 1983. 

13 PACKING AND PACKAGING 

13.1 Subland twist drill shall be packed as given 
in IS 5099 : 1983.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder* The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards.
